commitResults.messageTitle: Replace AB3 model with students and lessons
commitResults.messageBody:
The code was still AB3's address book of persons, which cannot hold
students, lessons, enrollments or payments.

Let's,
* replace Person with Student, Lesson and Enrollment, with separate ID
  counters, and rewrite the model, storage and UI around them
* replace the person commands with placeholders for add, delete, list,
  mark and filter, wired into the parser
* undo a command whose changes cannot be saved
* add shared test fixtures and tests for the new model and storage
* remove edit, find, clear and remark
* add empty guide headings for each command
Add Delete Command

Parse all four forms of add, treating s/ and l/ as an ID when it is
a whole number and as a new name or subject otherwise
Reject malformed input with the specification's messages
Implement unit tests for addCommand and AddCommandParser classes

commitResults.messageTitle: Enroll existing students in existing lessons
commitResults.messageBody:
add parsed its arguments but could not carry out any request.

Let's,
* enroll an existing student in an existing lesson, after checking
  that both exist, that the student is not already enrolled and that
  their levels match
* report the student's payment status in the success message
* run every check before changing anything, in the order the new
  forms of add will also need, so a failed command changes nothing
* test each failure, the order of the checks and the success cases

commitResults.messageTitle: Create new students and lessons in add
commitResults.messageBody:
add could only enroll existing students in existing lessons.

Let's,
* create a new student, a new lesson, or both, and enroll the student
  in the lesson, numbering students and lessons separately
* reject a new student or lesson that duplicates an existing one, and a
  new lesson that clashes with any existing lesson, allowing lessons
  that start exactly when another ends
* run every check before creating anything, so a failed command
  creates nothing and uses no ID
* check for duplicates before levels, and levels before clashes, so
  the user sees the most helpful message first
* test each form, each rule and the order in which the checks run

Add logging and assertions to add command
commitResults.messageBody:
A failed add left no trace in the log, and the parser read values it
had already checked with bare .get() calls, so a bug there would show
up as a NoSuchElementException far from its cause.

Let's,
* log the shape of each request and every rejection, using IDs only
  and never names or contact numbers
* reject null arguments in AddCommandParser.parse
* read required values through one requiredValue helper that asserts
  the value is present
* assert that an existing student or lesson is found exactly when it
  was given by ID
* assert that the student is enrolled after Model.enroll

commitResults.messageTitle: Add sequence diagram for the add command
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide has no diagram showing how add is parsed and
executed.

Let's,
* add AddSequenceDiagram.puml for
  execute("add s/Daniel Koh c/92223333 slv/Primary 6 l/1"): parsing,
  creating the AddCommand, the Model calls, and the result

The new null checks and the post-condition assertion have no tests.

Let's,
* test that parse and execute reject null arguments
* test that a Model whose enroll does nothing trips the post-condition
  assertion, skipping the test when assertions are turned off

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe the add feature in the Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The Add feature section is still a placeholder.

Let's,
* explain how AddCommandParser builds a StudentRef and a LessonRef
* list the order of the checks in AddCommand and why duplicates are
  checked before clashes
* embed the new sequence diagram
* record the design considerations behind the parser output, when new
  records are created, and the check order

commitResults.messageTitle: Share code between student and lesson classes
commitResults.messageBody:
StudentId and LessonId were identical, and so were UniqueStudentList
and UniqueLessonList apart from their names, so a fix to one had to
be repeated in the other.

Let's,
* add RecordId as the base of StudentId and LessonId, comparing
  classes so that a student ID never equals a lesson ID
* add UniqueIdList as the base of the two lists, leaving each
  subclass to say how to read an ID and what to throw when a record
  is not found
* test that IDs and lists of different kinds are never equal

commitResults.messageTitle: Simplify reading fields from the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
toModelType in the JSON adapters repeated "missing, invalid, build"
for every field, which made two of the methods longer than 35 lines.

Let's,
* add JsonFields with required and validated helpers
* use them in JsonAdaptedStudent, JsonAdaptedLesson and
  JsonAdaptedEnrollment, and move the timeslot and the last paid
  month into their own methods
* keep the order of the checks and every error message unchanged

commitResults.messageTitle: Stop logging names and contact numbers
commitResults.messageBody:
LogicManager logged every full command, MainWindow logged every
result and failed command, ModelManager logged the whole tracker and
AddressBookParser logged the arguments, so names and contact numbers
ended up in addressbook.log.

Let's,
* log only the command word in LogicManager and AddressBookParser
* log counts instead of the data in ModelManager
* log a fixed message or the error message in MainWindow
* test that add leaves no name or number in the log

commitResults.messageTitle: Add logging and assertions to TuiTracker
commitResults.messageBody:
TuiTracker changed the data without a trace, took an ID before it
rejected a null argument, and reported an enrollment of a missing
student as StudentNotFoundException, which looks like a user mistake.

Let's,
* log each change at fine level, using IDs only
* assert after an add or a delete that the lists are as expected
* reject null arguments before an ID is taken
* throw IllegalStateException for an enrollment of a missing student
* test that a null argument throws and uses no ID

commitResults.messageTitle: Split the long methods in the add command
commitResults.messageBody:
AddCommand.enroll and AddCommandParser.parseArguments each did a
whole series of checks and builds in one method, which made them
28 and 37 lines long and hard to read at a glance.

Let's,
* split AddCommand.enroll into the checks, the creation of what is
  new, the enrollment and the success message
* split checkForDuplicates into one method per kind of duplicate
* split AddCommandParser.parseArguments into one method per check,
  in the order the class comment lists them
* rename AddCommand.enroll to checkAndEnroll so that it no longer
  shares a name with Model.enroll

commitResults.messageTitle: Name constants and remove dead code
commitResults.messageBody:
IdGenerator.raiseTo was only called by its own test, the first ID was
written as a bare 1 in three places, and the number of decimal places
of a fee was written twice, once in the regex and once in setScale.

Let's,
* remove IdGenerator.raiseTo and its test
* add IdGenerator.FIRST_ID and use it in IdGenerator and in
  JsonSerializableTuiTracker
* add Fee.DECIMAL_PLACES and Fee.CURRENCY_SYMBOL
* use Objects.hash in IdGenerator.hashCode, like the other classes

commitResults.messageTitle: Match names and subjects ignoring case and spaces
commitResults.messageBody:
Duplicate checks compare names and subjects exactly, so "alice tan"
and "Alice  Tan" count as different students, and "mathematics" as a
different subject from "Mathematics" (#105, #106).

Let's,
* add StringUtil.toMatchingKey, which trims the text, collapses runs
  of spaces and lower-cases it
* add Name.isSameName and Subject.isSameSubject on top of it
* keep equals exact, so that edit can still change the letter case

Duplicate checks will need to treat "9222 3333" and "92223333" as the
same number, but contacts can only be compared exactly (#105, #109).

Let's,
* add Contact.digits, which keeps only the digits of a contact
* add Contact.isSameContact, which compares contacts by their digits
* keep equals exact, so that reformatting a number is still an edit

add only rejected a student or lesson that matched an existing one
exactly, so "alice tan" became a second Alice and a repeated lesson in
another letter case was reported as a clash. A namesake with a new
number was added without a word (#105, #106).

Let's,
* compare names, subjects and contacts with the new matching methods
  in TuiTracker's duplicate checks
* add Model#findStudentWithSameName
* enroll a same-name student with a different contact, ending the
  result with a note that names the existing student
* explain the duplicate rules in the User Guide and Developer Guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn instead of blocking on a level mismatch
commitResults.messageBody:
add refused to enrol a student in a lesson of another level, even
though a stronger student joining a higher-level class is normal, and
the error did not say what either level was (#108).

Let's,
* enrol the student anyway and end the result with a note that names
  both levels
* report a clash, not the level, when a new lesson has both problems
* update the User Guide example and error table, and the Developer
  Guide's checks and rationale

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept contacts with spaces and symbols
commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts had to be bare digits, so numbers written the usual way, such
as "9222 3333" or "+65 9222-3333", were rejected (#109).

Let's,
* accept digits with spaces, +, -, ( and ), counting only the digits
  towards the 3 to 15 limit
* keep the number as typed, and compare duplicates by digits only
* say what is allowed in the error message and the User Guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow common punctuation in names and subjects
commitResults.messageBody:
Names and subjects only allowed letters, numbers, spaces and hyphens,
so names such as "J. K. Rowling" or "Ravi s/o Kumar" and subjects such
as "Maths & Science" were rejected, with a message that did not say
which characters were allowed (#110, #107).

Let's,
* also allow . , ( ) & @ in names and subjects, and the apostrophe in
  names as before
* accept the words s/o and d/o in names, keeping / reserved elsewhere
* list the allowed characters and the length limit in the messages and
  the User Guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept short days, one-digit hours and free fees
commitResults.messageBody:
add rejected inputs a user would reasonably type: "d/Mon", "st/9:00"
and a fee of 0 for a free lesson. Ending at "24:00" was reported as a
generic bad end time (#113).

Let's,
* accept Mon, Tue, Tues, Wed, Thu, Thur, Thurs, Fri, Sat and Sun
* accept one-digit hours, storing them as HH:mm
* accept a fee of 0, and end the result with a note for a free lesson
* suggest 23:59 when a lesson is set to end at 24:00
* update the messages and both guides

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the lesson in the clash message
commitResults.messageBody:
When a new lesson overlapped another, add only said that it clashed
with "an existing lesson", so the user had to look through the
lessons to find which one (#112).

Let's,
* add Model#findClash, which returns the overlapping lesson with the
  lowest ID
* name that lesson's ID, subject, day and time in the clash message
* update the User Guide's error table

commitResults.messageTitle: Make add errors name the real problem
commitResults.messageBody:
Several typing slips gave messages that pointed at the wrong thing: a
missing space was reported as a missing parameter, an ID such as s/0
was read as a name, an ID followed by text as a new lesson, and a too
large ID as "must be a positive whole number" (#112).

Let's,
* report a parameter that is joined to another value without a space
* report a number that is not a valid ID before anything else
* say which value was read as a new student or lesson when parameters
  are missing, and suggest giving only the ID
* say that an ID given to add is too large instead of calling it
  invalid
* add these to the User Guide's error table

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain that lessons cannot run past midnight
commitResults.messageBody:
A lesson such as 23:00 to 01:00 was rejected with "enter a time later
than the start time", which does not tell the user that lessons
cannot cross midnight or what to do instead.

Let's,
* give a lesson that ends earlier than it starts its own message,
  which suggests splitting it into two lessons
* state the rule and the workaround in the User Guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Read prefixes ignoring case, keep s/o in names
commitResults.messageBody:
Prefixes were only found in lower case, so "S/1" was not a parameter,
and the "s/" or "d/" in a legal name such as "Ravi s/o Kumar" or
"Priya d/o Raj" was read as a new parameter (#107, #113).

Let's,
* find prefixes ignoring letter case
* leave the words s/o and d/o inside the value they belong to
* say in the User Guide that prefixes can be in any case

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept command words in any case
commitResults.messageBody:
Command words were case-sensitive, so "ADD" or "List" gave "Unknown
command." even though nothing else depends on the case (#113).

Let's,
* lower-case the command word before choosing the command
* say in the User Guide that command words can be in any case

commitResults.messageTitle: Wrap long text in results and cards
commitResults.messageBody:
Long text was cut off: a lesson with many students showed only the
first few, ending in "...", a long name ran past the edge of the
result box, and a long name on a card was cut short (#111, #114).

Let's,
* wrap the result box, and the names, subjects and lists on cards
* size the card column to the card's width, so wrapped text is not
  measured as if it were 150 pixels wide
* make each list cell take the list's width, so cards do not grow
  wider than the list

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep typed names out of the log on errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Error messages now repeat what was typed, such as "s/Daniel Koh was
read as a new student", and both the add parser and MainWindow logged
them, so names and contact numbers reached addressbook.log again.

Let's,
* log only that add's arguments were rejected, not the message
* log only the kind of error in MainWindow
* test that rejected commands leave no name or number in the log

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept only phone-number shapes in contacts
commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts accepted any mix of digits, spaces, +, -, ( and ) with no
length limit, so "+-+-((1))--2--3" or a number padded with 70 spaces
was stored as typed.

Let's,
* allow a + only at the start, and one space or hyphen between groups
  of digits, with a group optionally in brackets
* cap a contact at 25 characters
* describe the exact format in the message and the User Guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Bring the add section of the guide up to date
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide still described add as it was before the fixes:
the parser's list of checks missed three new ones, the notes paragraph
missed the free-lesson note, and the glossary said a fee must be
positive and a student's level must match the lesson's.

Let's,
* list all eight parser checks in their actual order
* name all three notes, in the order they appear
* update the glossary entries for the lesson fee and level matching

commitResults.messageTitle: Document s/o and d/o in student names
commitResults.messageBody:
Names can now contain the words s/o and d/o, but neither the error
message nor the User Guide said so, so a user would not know that
"Ravi s/o Kumar" is allowed.

Let's,
* mention s/o and d/o in the invalid-name message, with an example
* say in the User Guide that they can be part of a name, and that a
  name cannot start with the single word O

commitResults.messageTitle: Test add with s/o and d/o names end to end
commitResults.messageBody:
The tokenizer and Name tests each cover half of the s/o support,
but no test parses a whole add command with such a name.

Let's,
* add a parser test for Ravi S/O Kumar and Priya d/o Raj
Improve list edit quality
Revert "Improve list edit quality"
Restore edit command validation updates

commitResults.messageTitle: Mention midnight only for late lesson times
commitResults.messageBody:
Any end time before the start time got the message about lessons
past midnight, so swapped times like 17:00 to 16:00 were told to
split the lesson, and an end of 00:00 was never told to use 23:59.

Let's,
* keep that message when the lesson would last 6 hours or less
  past midnight
* ask for a later end time in every other case
* suggest 23:59 for an end time of 00:00, as for 24:00
* add a guide example for swapped times
Improve defensive coding and logging for list and edit commands

commitResults.messageTitle: Share the end time messages with edit
commitResults.messageBody:
The rules that pick the end time message sit inside the add parser,
so edit, which only knows its final times later, cannot use them.

Let's,
* move the rules into Timeslot#messageForInvalidEnd
* call it from ParserUtil#parseEndTime
Use shared end-time messages for edit command
